title: PowerPoint on Mac: reference webpages when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: The briefing accurately reports the launched Mac capability and distinguishes documented web-search controls from their unconfirmed reach over this presentation flow. The admin link is correct but should include the remaining route into Cloud Policy configuration.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Microsoft's release note says the web-source capability respects web content security and privacy standards.
claims.quote: This update enables Copilot to gather relevant information from the web and use referenced sources while respecting web content security and privacy standards.

claims.claim: The release note instructs users to ask Copilot for a presentation on a topic benefiting from current web information.
claims.quote: Ask Copilot to create a presentation on a topic that would benefit from current web information.

claims.claim: The release note instructs users to review generated slides and source references.
claims.quote: Review the generated slides and source references.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: No dedicated Microsoft Learn page for this specific Mac webpage-reference feature was found beyond the release note.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint reference webpages presentation Agent Mode Mac 555893; Copilot PowerPoint reference webpages admin disable setting API default prerequisites. Opened release-notes, manage-public-web-access, configure-copilot-admin-center and copilot-overview; no dedicated feature page found.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap description nor this release-note entry says users can paste webpage addresses.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint reference webpages presentation Agent Mode Mac 555893. Read roadmap 555893 and the full Mac entry in release-notes; the entry asks for a topic benefiting from current web information but specifies no pasted URL workflow.

claims.claim: The release-note entry for this change does not use the words Agent Mode.
claims.quote: Searched: release notes 555893 Previously. Read the entire Reference web sources [Mac] entry in release-notes, including Details and Try this; Agent Mode does not occur in that entry.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Copilot web search derives a search query from the prompt and sends it to the Bing search service.
claims.quote: Based on these terms, Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Generated web-search queries exclude the entire prompt unless it is very short.
claims.quote: The following information isn't included in the generated search query sent to the Bing search service: ... The user's entire prompt, unless the prompt is very short (for example, "local weather")

claims.claim: Generated web-search queries exclude entire Microsoft 365 files.
claims.quote: The following information isn't included in the generated search query sent to the Bing search service: ... Entire Microsoft 365 files (for example, emails or documents) or files uploaded into Copilot

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A generated query can be informed by data in an open Microsoft 365 document when the user prompts Copilot inside an app.
claims.quote: However, it may also be informed by data within a Microsoft 365 document ... When a user enters a prompt into Copilot inside a Microsoft 365 application (for example, writing a prompt into Copilot in Microsoft Word while a relevant document is open).

claims.claim: The Bing search service operates separately from Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: The Bing search service operates separately from Microsoft 365 and has different data-handling practices.

claims.claim: Generated queries sent to Bing are handled under different terms from Microsoft 365 data.
claims.quote: The web search queries generated by Copilot and sent to Bing are subject to the Microsoft Services Agreement between each user and Microsoft, together with the Microsoft Privacy Statement.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the feature-specific default on arrival, represented as unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint reference webpages admin disable setting API default prerequisites; PowerPoint web sources default. Read roadmap 555893, its complete release-note entry and manage-public-web-access; no feature-specific default or required enablement action is stated.

claims.claim: The release note says users previously could not directly incorporate live web information as source material within Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: Previously, users could not directly incorporate live web information as source material within Copilot in PowerPoint.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: For commercial web search generally, an unconfigured Allow web search in Copilot policy leaves it available unless the optional connected experiences policy is Disabled.
claims.quote: If the IT admin doesn't configure the Allow web search in Copilot policy, web search will be available to users in both Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat, unless the IT admin has set the Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office policy to Disabled.

claims.claim: Copilot sends the user's client IP address with a web-search request to Bing.
claims.quote: When Copilot sends a web search request to the Bing search service, it also sends the user's client IP address, which Bing uses to help localize results, such as nearby weather and events.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Data Protection Addendum does not apply to generated web-search queries.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum (DPA) doesn't apply to the use of generated web search queries in Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Chat, or the Bing search service.

claims.claim: HIPAA compliance does not apply to generated web-search queries.
claims.quote: Also, HIPAA compliance and the EU Data Boundary don't apply to generated search queries.

claims.claim: The EU Data Boundary does not apply to generated web-search queries.
claims.quote: Also, HIPAA compliance and the EU Data Boundary don't apply to generated search queries.

claims.claim: The roadmap description and this release-note entry describe no actions beyond producing the presentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint reference webpages presentation Agent Mode Mac 555893. Read roadmap 555893 and the complete Mac release-note entry; both describe presentation creation with web sources, not other actions.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The general Allow web search in Copilot Cloud Policy controls web search for users or user groups across the tenant.
claims.quote: This policy allows IT admins to either turn on or turn off web search for users or user groups across the tenant they manage ... This policy applies to both Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Users can turn web search off themselves when the administrator allows it.
claims.quote: If the IT admin turns on web search for Microsoft Copilot users, those users still have the option to turn off web search by using the Web content toggle.

claims.claim: General Copilot web-search query logging supports auditing generated queries.
claims.quote: Web search query logging is available so that admins can perform search, audit, and eDiscovery on the exact web search queries Copilot derived from the user's prompt.

claims.claim: General Copilot web-search query logging supports eDiscovery of generated queries.
claims.quote: Web search query logging is available so that admins can perform search, audit, and eDiscovery on the exact web search queries Copilot derived from the user's prompt.

claims.quote: For United States government customers using Microsoft 365 (or Office 365) Government Community Cloud (GCC) or DoD offerings: Web search is available, but is turned off by default.

claims.claim: Copilot web search generally is off by default for DoD.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > Data access > Web search for Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat reaches the documented Cloud Policy shortcut.
claims.quote: Follow the link from Copilot settings to create an Allow web search in Copilot cloud policy in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
claims.fix: The printed route is a valid shortcut but stops before configuration. Append to controls[0].note and the rendered note: 'Follow this shortcut to Microsoft 365 Apps admin center: Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy alongside the existing sources; its creation steps give the remaining route.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors with mode applyOnce can apply the specified desired-state web-search baseline.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors ... An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch baseline resource uses properties.value "0" to enable web search.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch" ... "properties": { "value": "0" }; Controls web search. 0 enables it in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The allowwebsearch resource value "1" disables web search in both Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: Controls web search. 0 enables it in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. 1 disables it in both.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The allowwebsearch resource value "2" disables web search only in Work mode.
claims.quote: 2 disables it in Microsoft 365 Copilot Work mode while enabling it in Microsoft 365 Copilot Web mode and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The Graph TCM route for applying this setting is preview.
claims.quote: Tenant Configuration Management (TCM) drift remediation and applyOnce monitors change workload configuration on behalf of the signed-in administrator. These capabilities are available in preview through Microsoft Graph beta.

claims.claim: TCM supports these Copilot settings only in tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: A group-level policy configuring the same setting causes TCM operations for that resource to fail.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.
